persons.name: Ravendradeva
persons.evidence: bhikṣuravendradeveti ācāryasya … pustaka pratimā ca vajtaghaṇṭāyugāni ca | pra(!)ñcarakṣā(bhi)yānaś ca … pratiṣthā kṛtaḥ … ācārya sthavira ravendradevasya yatpuṇyaṃ

date.as_written: trayo dhikesītisate gate abde māse jyeṣṭe kṛtakṛṣṇapakṣake | aikādaśī somaprasasyasaṃjñake; samvat a 0[(8)] 3 jya///

purpose: Consecration (pratiṣṭhā) by Ravendradeva of the book together with an image, a pair of vajra and ghaṇṭā, and a Cakrasaṃvara image; merit for his guru, mother and father, and all beings (gurumātāpitā …; mātāpitṛṇāṃ sarvasatvānāṃ).
notes: Two dates: an earlier one on exp. 69b (samvat a 0((8))2 = NS 182, Bhādrapada kṛṣṇa 13, end of the Mahāmāyūrī section) and the final one NS 183 Jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa 11 given both in verse (trayo-adhika-aśīti-śate) and in figures; the final date is recorded above. Conflict in the king's name: the verse colophon on exp. 122 names Śaṅkaradeva as reigning, while the prose colophon on exp. 123 (same year NS 183) names (Pradyumna)kāmadeva, written corruptly as śrī(pajuna)kāmadevasya; the catalogue gives only Pradyumnakāmadeva. NS 183 = 1063 CE fits Pradyumnakāmadeva's known reign; Śaṅkaradeva is otherwise attested c. NS 189–202, so the verse may be a later/dislocated addition or the manuscript may be composite. Mānadeva in 'śrīmanmānadevasya vihāre' is part of the vihāra name (Mānadeva-vihāra, usually identified with Cakravihāra/Cuka Bāhā, Patan), not a person involved in this copy, hence not listed and place left unnormalized. No scribe is named; 'kṛtā†nipha†///ni' is too damaged to yield a name. Ravendradeva's guru and parents are mentioned as merit recipients but not named. Catalogue date 'NS 182, 183' matches the colophon.
